e-4439.problem:
Calculate the minor of the entry $b_{21}$ in the matrix

$$
[\begin{aligned}10 & 1 & 5 \\ 3 & 6 & 8 \\ 4 & 7 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$
e-4439.worked_solution:
The minor of $b_{21} = 3$ (second row, first column) is the determinant of the remaining entries when the column and row containing $3$ are removed: 

$$
[\begin{aligned}∗ & 1 & 5 \\ 3 & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & 7 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the minor of $b_{21}=3$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}det[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 7 & 2\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 7 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot 2-5\cdot 7 \\  & =2-35 \\  & =-33.\end{aligned}
$$

e-4440.problem:
What is the minor of $c_{22}$ in the matrix

$$
[\begin{aligned}7x & 0 & -3y \\ 1 & x+2y & 4 \\ -y & 0 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$
e-4440.worked_solution:
First, we remove the second row and second column: 

$$
[\begin{aligned}7x & ∗ & -3y \\ ∗ & x+2y & ∗ \\ -y & ∗ & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Next, we calculate the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det[\begin{aligned}7x & -3y \\ -y & 5\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}7x & -3y \\ -y & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =7x\cdot 5-(-3y)\cdot (-y) \\  & =35x-3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

e-4441.knowledge_point: Solving for an Unknown Given the Value of a Minor
e-4441.problem:
Given that the minor of $a_{23}$ is $5,$ find all the possible values of $k$ in the matrix

$$
[\begin{aligned}k & 3 & -1 \\ -5 & 2 & 7 \\ -1 & 2k & -6\end{aligned}]
$$
e-4441.worked_solution:
First, we remove the second row and third column:

$$
[\begin{aligned}k & 3 & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & 7 \\ -1 & 2k & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

The minor of $a_{23}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}det[\begin{aligned}k & 3 \\ -1 & 2k\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}k & 3 \\ -1 & 2k\end{aligned}| \\  & =k\cdot 2k-3\cdot (-1) \\  & =2{k}^{2}+3.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that the minor of $a_{23}$ is $5,$ so we must have:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{k}^{2}+3 & =5 \\ 2{k}^{2} & =2 \\ {k}^{2} & =1 \\ k & =\pm 1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $k=-1$ and $k=1.$

To evaluate the minor of ${f}_{32},$ we remove the third row and second column: 

$$
F=[\begin{aligned}y & ∗ & 1 \\ 2 & ∗ & 4 \\ ∗ & 8 & ∗\end{aligned}]

So, the minor of ${f}_{32}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}[\begin{aligned}y & 1 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}y & 1 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =y\cdot 4-1\cdot 2 \\  & =4y-2.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that the minor of ${f}_{32}$ is $10$, so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4y-2 & =10 \\ 4y & =12 \\ y & =3.\end{aligned}
